svg.title: Falcon Lens architecture in three layers, with the tools it runs on
svg.desc: Three stacked layers. Voice layer · "Hey Falcon": Browser microphone, Whisper speech to text, Wake phrase and intent, Amazon Polly · Zayd, Kokoro, Earcons. The two AI agents: T0 · Known reports, T1 · Address and domain, T2 · Isolated browser, T3 · AI second look, Deterministic arbiter, Verdict and reasons, Correlation, Incident rules, LangGraph StateGraph, Incident and audit log, Human approval. Platform: FastAPI, MCP server, STIX 2.1 export, Next.js web app, Redis Streams, PostgreSQL, pgvector, Playwright sandbox, Egress proxy, Model router, Claude API, Ollama, Inkling, Qwen, DSPy, OpenTelemetry, Arize Phoenix, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, Caddy, Cloudflare Tunnel, Docker Compose. A numbered request path runs through them, in this order. You say "Hey Falcon" and ask for a check. The browser records one short clip. Then: Whisper turns the clip into text on our own machine. The audio is not stored. Then: Fixed rules find the wake phrase and what you asked. The check then starts. Then: Baseer, T0: is this already known? A recent verdict, a scam-list match or a verified official site. Then: T1 studies the address and the domain, and a measured classifier scores them. Then: T2 opens the page once, passively, in an isolated browser and compares it with the real brand. Then: T3, unclear cases only: a bounded model gathers a little more evidence. It cannot change the score. Then: The deterministic arbiter weighs the evidence. Fixed code sets the verdict, not the model. Then: The verdict and its reasons reach your screen, and are spoken aloud. Then: Every finished check is announced on the event bus (Redis Streams). Then: Dir' links related checks: the same brand, the same page or the same domain pattern. Then: Fixed rules decide that the group is an incident, and how severe it is. Then: A LangGraph graph gathers context, summarises and proposes actions. Its state is checkpointed. Then: The incident and every action are written to an append-only audit log. Then: Anything that would leave the system stays a draft until a person approves it. Logos belong to their owners; shown to identify the tools used.
svg.text: One request, three layers: follow the numbers. Every box is shipped code, shown with the tool it runs on.
Speech is understood on our own machine. Answers are spoken from clips prepared in advance.
Baseer judges one input. Dir' watches every check around the clock.
The services both agents run on, in one Docker Compose stack.
Logos belong to their owners; shown to identify the tools used. Text badges mark tools whose logo is not vendored. Dashed boxes are model steps.
